evals.prompt: Please restyle our marketing page to match Acme Corp's brand. I tried to pull their internal brand guide PDF from their SharePoint but it's SSO-gated and I can't get you access.
evals.expected_output: Skill should NOT default to approximating Acme's brand colors/fonts from general knowledge. Should propose checking Acme's public website (acme.com) CSS/HTML as a fetchable proxy for the same ground truth, fetch it (curl/WebFetch), extract real hex codes and font-family declarations, and only fall back to approximation (clearly flagged, per-value) if no public artifact exists at all.

evals.prompt: I need to build a client that matches VendorX's API contract, but their API docs page requires a paid account I don't have.
evals.expected_output: Skill should suggest checking for alternative public sources of the same contract before guessing: a published OpenAPI/Swagger file, a public GitHub SDK/client repo that reveals the real request/response shapes, a public Postman collection, or archived docs. Should not fabricate endpoint shapes from generic REST conventions without flagging them as unverified.

evals.prompt: Align our app's styling to [University]'s branding. Here's a link to their internal design system doc.
evals.expected_output: Skill should first try the given link. If reachable, extract real values directly (fetch the doc, don't summarize from a screenshot alone). If blocked, skill should propose fetching the university's own public website CSS as the next-best verifiable proxy before offering any 'best-effort from memory' fallback, and should not proceed with a full implementation on guessed values without explicitly listing which specific values are unverified and getting confirmation first.

evals.prompt: I already implemented a rebrand based on my general knowledge of how the target company's brand usually looks, without checking their actual website. Is that OK to ship?
evals.expected_output: Skill should flag this as the anti-pattern it documents: general/trained knowledge is not a substitute for a verifiable live source when one is reachable (their public website almost always is). Should recommend verifying every asserted value (colors, fonts, shape language) against the actual live site/CSS before shipping, even though implementation already happened — better to catch it before deployment than after a user has to point it out.

evals.prompt: I'm in plan mode, about to design an integration that needs to mirror Stripe's checkout flow UX. My research so far only covered our own codebase.
evals.expected_output: Skill should flag the gap: repo-only exploration is insufficient for an external-alignment task. Plan-mode Phase 1 research should explicitly include inspecting Stripe's actual live checkout flow/public docs as its own research step, with the same weight as internal codebase exploration, before the plan is finalized.
